topic: Restraint as power: refusing to collect grudges

story.title: Marcus Aurelius burns Avidius Cassius's letters unread

quotes: The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.

slides.headline: HE BURNED THE LETTERS
slides.body: The emperor's most powerful move was the one he refused to make.

visual.text: Avidius Cassius, one of Rome's best generals, hears Marcus is dead and claims the throne. He is wrong. Marcus is alive.

slides.headline: The rebellion collapses
slides.body: Within three months Cassius is killed by his own officers. His letters reveal who backed him.

items: His own men turn on him

slides.headline: Marcus burns them unread
slides.body: He never learned which senators betrayed him. He chose not to.

slides.headline: Grudges are a tax
slides.body: Every enemy you track costs attention you could spend leading.

items: Someone undermined you: note the lesson, drop the file

slides.headline: Restraint is leverage
items: Power that is not used still lands

slides.headline: FOLLOW FOR DAILY STOIC POWER
slides.body: Think like Plato. Speak like a leader. Influence like a CEO.

caption:
He held proof of who betrayed him. He burned it unread.

In 175 AD the general Avidius Cassius tried to take Rome. When the revolt failed, his letters reached Marcus Aurelius. Marcus burned them without reading a line.

That is stoic leadership: power you hold back still speaks. Marcus Aurelius knew grudges cost the one who keeps them.

Save this for the next time someone crosses you at work.

#stoicism #leadership #marcusaurelius

beats.headline: HE BURNED THE EVIDENCE

media.credit: File:Marcus Aurelius Capitoline Hill September 2015-1.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: He held the name of every traitor in Rome. And he burned them.

media.credit: File:Trajan's Column - NMR - panel 057 A.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: 175 AD. Rome's best general hears the emperor is dead.
So Avidius Cassius does the unthinkable. He crowns himself.

beats.headline: But Marcus was alive

media.credit: File:Head Marcus Aurelius archmus Heraklion.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: One problem. Marcus Aurelius is alive.

media.title: File:Jean-Léon Gérôme - The Death of Caesar - Walters 37884.jpg
media.credit: File:Jean-Léon Gérôme - The Death of Caesar - Walters 37884.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: Within 3 months, Cassius is dead. Killed by his own officers.

media.credit: File:Roman Fresco showing a young man with a scroll labelled "Plato", from House of the Apartment, Pompeii (48452294242).jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: Then a chest arrives. The rebel's letters. Every senator who backed him, named.

media.credit: File:Ernest Joseph Bailly - The Vestal Virgins Handing over the Testament of Emperor Augustus to the Roman Senate - 2005-O - Museum of Fine Arts Ghent (MSK).jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: One look, and Marcus could purge the whole Senate.

beats.headline: He never read a line

media.title: File:Cole Thomas The Course of Empire Destruction 1836.jpg
media.credit: File:Cole Thomas The Course of Empire Destruction 1836.jpg (Wikimedia Commons)

beats.voice: He throws the letters into the fire. Unread.

beats.voice: So when someone crosses you, don't keep the file. Keep the room.
